`headers.jsonl` and `proof_records.jsonl` are generated by
`tools/generate_header_fixtures.py` against mmx-node
`ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`. No reference source, database or wallet
is modified. The oracle links the existing native libraries and calls original
BlockHeader hashing/content hashing/static validity/authentication and OG/NFT
proof methods directly.

To expose exact header preimages, the generator copies the original
BlockHeader::calc_hash body into a subclass, replacing only the return type and
`return hash_t(buffer)` with `return buffer`. Its virtual get_type_hash returns
the original object's type identity. Context checks copy the unchanged scalar
section of Node::validate, from parent lookup through difficulty minima, into a
small harness with a fixed trusted parent. This covers linkage, height,
space-fork limits, timestamp bounds and difficulty minima; economics/body checks
remain covered by the block fixtures.

Header rows contain a name, original VNX record, expected hash preimage/hash,
content hash, native static-validity result, farmer authentication result and
context outcome. Snapshot rows provide ChainParams and parent header wires;
subsequent `seed` rows reuse those fields. `ERR` records a native exception.
`SKIP` avoids invoking native hashing/authentication on null proof dereferences;
static validity still rejects those rows, and Rust hashing returns an error.

Both actual Block and BlockHeader identities are exercised, along with native
Block::get_header slicing that retains the original stored hash/signature.
Header validity deliberately excludes Block::is_valid body checks, which have
their own fixtures. Authentication is checked separately from static validity.
Proof rows compare structural validity, record hash, challenge/coordinate hash,
plot ID calculation and the original ProofOfSpaceOG/NFT::validate identity check.

These are not proof-of-space/VDF work fixtures. A valid shape, matching plot ID
or authentic farmer signature alone does not establish proof quality, filters,
difficulty transitions, weights or NFT reward-target correctness.
